procedure.step: The Ministry of Foreign Trade provides the Certificate of Origin for India e-service to submit the application and required documents.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 for an invoice value up to AED 100000.
The competent authority shall issue the Certificate of Origin prior to, at, or within five working days of the date of exportation.

The Indian importer claims preferential tariff treatment when filing the bill of entry, holding origin information under CAROTAR 2020 rules, with electronic certificates reportedly accepted and uploaded to e-Sanchit.
The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for no less than five years starting from the end of the year of the date of issue.

caveats.note: Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
